clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation overlap maps were performed using permutation testing (10,000 permutations) to derive an empirical null distribution of the overlap difference map. This was done at voxel, tract, region, and network levels.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study provides a comprehensive multiscale atlas of white matter volume (WMV) alterations in psychiatric disorders, identifying a general transdiagnostic reduction in WMV alongside disorder-specific patterns of dysconnectivity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: A transdiagnostic pattern of lower WMV was observed, with diagnosis-specific patterns of greater WMV. The spatial distribution of extreme WMV deviations was heterogeneous, showing greatest convergence in schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder. Individualized deviation maps implicated distinct dysconnectivity patterns for each disorder.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Cross-sectional design limits inferences about longitudinal progression. 2. Analysis was restricted to adults, limiting generalizability to younger populations. 3. The sample was largely of European ancestry, which may limit generalizability to other populations. 4. A static measure of dysconnectivity was used, potentially missing dynamic brain function. 5. Clinical data was limited, preventing analysis of relationships between WMV alterations and symptom severity or treatment response.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, we used a cross-sectional design, which precludes any inferences about the longitudinal progression of WMV alterations. Second, our analysis was restricted to adults...Third, although we aggregated data from many sites, the sample was largely comprised of individuals of European ancestry...Fourth, we used a static measure of dysconnectivity...Finally, the clinical data were limited in scope...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study employed a multiscale analysis, investigating deviations at voxel, tract, region, and network levels. It also utilized an independent cohort (HCP) for diffusion tractography to map structural pathways associated with WMV deviations, a technique similar to lesion-network mapping.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a large-scale study applying normative modeling to a multi-site aggregated dataset of over 2,700 individuals to investigate white matter volume (WMV) alterations across six major psychiatric disorders. A key strength and innovation is its multiscale approach, analyzing deviations at the voxel, tract, region, and network levels. The study also uniquely combines the normative model deviations with structural connectivity data from an independent cohort to infer 'dysconnectivity' patterns. The findings point to both shared (transdiagnostic) and disorder-specific neurobiological signatures.
